# Load required libraries
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

# Load the msleep dataset
```{r}
data(msleep)
```
# ============================================================================
# Task 1: Create and customize a scatterplot
# ============================================================================
# Create a scatterplot of sleep_total vs bodywt (body weight).
# Customize your plot with:
# - A point character (pch) of your choice
# - Blue colored points
# - Axis labels: "Body Weight (kg)" for x-axis and "Total Sleep (hours)" for y-axis
# - A border style of your choice (bty)

# Your code here:
```{r}
# Create a scatterplot of total sleep versus body weight
plot(msleep$sleep_total ~ msleep$bodywt,
     pch = 16,
     col = "blue",
     xlab = "Body Weight (kg)",
     ylab = "Total Sleep (hours)",
     bty = "L")
```



# ============================================================================
# Task 2: Make a histogram
# ============================================================================
# Create a histogram of the brainwt (brain weight) variable.
# Customize your histogram with:
# - A color of your choice (col)
# - An appropriate x-axis label
# - A descriptive title using the main argument

# Your code here:
```{r}
# Create a boxplot comparing total sleep across different diet types
boxplot(msleep$sleep_total ~ as.factor(msleep$vore),
        col = rainbow(4),
        xlab = "Diet Type",
        ylab = "Total Sleep (hours)",
        main = "Total Sleep by Diet Type")
```



# ============================================================================
# Task 3: Create a boxplot comparing groups
# ============================================================================
# Create a boxplot showing sleep_total for each vore type (diet).
# Customize your boxplot with:
# - Different colors for each box (hint: use rainbow() or choose specific colors)
# - Appropriate axis labels
# - Convert vore to a factor using as.factor()

# Your code here:
```{r}
# Create a boxplot comparing total sleep across different diet types
boxplot(msleep$sleep_total ~ as.factor(msleep$vore),
        col = rainbow(4),
        xlab = "Diet Type",
        ylab = "Total Sleep (hours)",
        main = "Total Sleep by Diet Type")
```



# ============================================================================
# Bonus Challenge (Optional)
# ============================================================================
# Create a scatterplot of any two continuous variables from msleep.
# Add a line of best fit using abline() and lm().
# Color points based on a condition you define (like we did with sleep_total >= 17
# in the tutorial), and add a legend to explain the colors.

# Your code here:
```{r}
# Color points based on whether total sleep is at least 17 hours
msleep$colors <- ifelse(msleep$sleep_total >= 17, "red", "black")

# Create a scatterplot of total sleep versus body weight
plot(msleep$sleep_total ~ msleep$bodywt,
     pch = 16,
     col = msleep$colors,
     xlab = "Body Weight (kg)",
     ylab = "Total Sleep (hours)")

# Add a line of best fit using a linear model
abline(lm(msleep$sleep_total ~ msleep$bodywt))

# Add a legend explaining the colors
legend("topright",
       legend = c("17+ hours", "Less than 17 hours"),
       col = c("red", "black"),
       pch = 16)
```
